newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts end little changed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts end little changed in dull trade.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities were little changed in dull trade on Friday while the call money market was inactive, dealers said.
They said trade in securities was limited as market players awaited a clearer picture on liquidity after advance tax payments by companies.
The last date for payment of advance tax by companies is March 15 and analysts estimate the amount to be between 30 billion and 50 billion rupees.
Dealers said the ouftlows could lead to a temporary tightening of liquidity, pushing up call money rates.

"Market players are not taking trading positions because of the fear that rates may go up." said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Further with the year-end also coming up, banks are not prepared to build up positions."
The financial year ends on March 31.

Dealers said the 12.50 percent 2004 governn Friday at 96.55 rupees against its last traded price of 96.53, the 13.25 percent 1997 nudged up to 101.31 from 101.30 and the 13.70, percent 1999 eased to 102.83 from 102.85.
"Most of the trade was in medium-term securities," said a money market dealer. "Traded volumes were 870 million against yesterday's 610 million."

Dealers said no deals were reported in overnight call money as it was the fortnightly reporting day for banks. Banks do not normally borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Dealers said three-day repos were struck at 5.5-6.0 percent while repos for the fortninght was at seven percent.
They said call money was likely to open around six percent.
